findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/IsTensorProduct.lean:415 `theorem IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul (s : S) (m : M) : h.equiv (s ⊗ₜ m) = s • f m := rfl` — proved by `rfl`, so the property named in the docstring holds for any `f`.
findings.fix: Reword: the field asserts that the canonical ℝ-linear map `ℝ ⊗[ℤ] N → V` determined by `1 ⊗ₜ n ↦ i n` is a linear equivalence (equivalently, `IsBaseChange`); injectivity and full real span are its consequences, not its statement.
findings.issue: The `IsIntegralLattice` docstring says "The base-change condition says that the scalar extension sends each pure tensor `1 ⊗ₜ n` to the corresponding lattice vector `i n`." That equation is definitionally true for the canonical map and carries no content; the actual content of `IsBaseChange ℝ i.toIntLinearMap` is that the canonical map `ℝ ⊗[ℤ] N → V` is bijective. A reader is told the central hypothesis is something vacuous.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/IsTensorProduct.lean:390 `theorem TensorProduct.isBaseChange : IsBaseChange S (TensorProduct.mk R S M 1)`; grep of the diff shows no `example`, `instance`, or theorem producing an `IsIntegralLattice` other than `of_equiv`.
findings.fix: Add one non-degenerate witness, e.g. for finite free `N` the map `(TensorProduct.mk ℤ ℝ N 1).toAddMonoidHom : N →+ ℝ ⊗[ℤ] N` is an integral lattice via `TensorProduct.isBaseChange ℤ N ℝ`.
findings.issue: No witness that `IsIntegralLattice` is inhabited. The only constructor, `of_equiv` (line 376), demands the scalar-extension equivalence itself, so every consequence in the PR (`injective`, `span_range_eq_top`, `finrank_eq_finrank`, `isDiscrete_range`, `isZLattice_range`) is unexercised on a concrete example; the predicate's faithfulness is not falsifiable from inside the PR.

findings.evidence: Lattice.lean:347-357 — the local attribute and `variable` block sit before `end TauCeti` at line 357, while `V₀` and all normed-space lemmas are introduced at line 454 onward; the instance body is literally `NormedSpace.toModule`.
findings.fix: Delete lines 347–355; `NormedSpace.toModule` already supplies `Module ℝ V₀`. If some elaboration genuinely needed a priority tweak, scope it with `attribute [local instance]` in the section where it is used.
findings.issue: `private noncomputable instance moduleOfNormedSpace (E) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] : Module ℝ E := NormedSpace.toModule` duplicates Mathlib's `NormedSpace.toModule`. `private` hides the name but not the instance registration, so every downstream file importing this module resolves `Module ℝ E` for normed spaces through this later-declared duplicate — the `Module ℝ V₀` appearing in the statements of `isDiscrete_range`/`isZLattice_range` is this one, not Mathlib's. The accompanying `attribute [local instance 1001] NormedAddCommGroup.toAddCommGroup AddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid` (line 347) and the `variable` line 351 are inside `namespace TauCeti`, which closes at line 357 before any of the affected declarations, so they have no effect at all.

summary: The integral-lattice definition and its consequences are mathematically faithful to the roadmap's pinned convention, but the structure's docstring describes the base-change field as a definitionally trivial equation, nothing in the PR exhibits an inhabitant of the new predicate, and a private-but-globally-registered `Module ℝ E` instance duplicates `NormedSpace.toModule`.
